description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Checkov fixture whose failed checks carry line information that is present but unusable. Every value was derived by reading the fixture, the recorded runner metadata and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, and every anchor fact was checked against the pinned tree at 59b8a4489c878fa3a9aa6b7fbae760f2fc80eb9d -- never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. What makes this fixture unlike every other non-integer-start-line fixture in the tree is structural: checkov is the only tool whose start_line comes from inside an array -- file_line_range[0] -- rather than from a scalar field, so the array itself can be the wrong shape and not merely its first element the wrong type. Four distinct defects and one legitimate absence therefore sit side by side in one document, and separating them is the whole of this file's subject.
scanner_class_note: Fixed for this tool by AAP 0.5.4's class table and carried unchanged on every row. It does not vary with check_type, with the reporting framework or with record content; trivy is the single tool whose class is decided per record, from the section the record was read from. A rejected record carries no scanner_class at all, because it produces no row.

fixture.top_level_form_note: A single report object -- the form a Checkov artifact takes when one framework reports. The multi-framework array form is covered by oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/checkov-alt-shape.json and is not re-covered here: this fixture's subject is the file_line_range field, and testing one thing at a time is what makes a failure attributable.
fixture.summary_note: The report's own summary object, quoted as the fixture carries it. It is never used as the record count: the count unit below is the one normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction. It happens to agree with that count here, and agreement is not the same as authority.
fixture.derived_from: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/checkov.json, a byte-for-byte capture of harness/artifacts/raw/checkov.json (sha256 91e9cf3cc81e17786af239cba88aa770ae96351a719bd6193ec19962cc238643, 8380 bytes, 6 failed checks) -- so an index into that fixture and the same index into the raw artifact name the same record
fixture.derivation: A negative fixture is derived from the captured one rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated as a derivation. One of the six failed checks is unmodified captured output: /results/failed_checks/0 is identical to the raw artifact's failed_checks[4] and to the positive fixture's failed_checks[4] on all 28 fields. The other five are each derived from a captured record by changing that record's file_line_range and nothing else -- four to a defective shape and one by removing the field outright.
fixture.captured_provenance: Established by canonical-JSON comparison of every field of every record, not by eye. /results/failed_checks/1 agrees with the raw artifact's failed_checks[5] on 27 of its 28 fields, differing only in file_line_range, whose captured value [1, 71] is replaced by ["20", 20]. /results/failed_checks/2 agrees with raw failed_checks[0] on 27 of 28, its captured [32, 36] replaced by the empty array []. /results/failed_checks/3 agrees with raw failed_checks[1] on 27 of 28, its captured [1, 46] replaced by the number 20. /results/failed_checks/4 agrees with raw failed_checks[2] on 27 of 28, its captured [34, 37] replaced by the string "20". /results/failed_checks/5 agrees with raw failed_checks[3] on every field it carries and has 27 fields to that record's 28, its captured [1, 47] removed rather than replaced. So in every case the sole defect -- or the sole absence -- is the record's statement about its own line range: check_id, check_name, severity, file_path, file_abs_path, repo_file_path, check_result and every other field are the tool's own output. That isolation is the point: a fixture that changed a second field could not attribute the outcome to the line range.
fixture.buckets_are_additions: The passed_checks, skipped_checks and parsing_errors this fixture carries are additions rather than captured content, and stating so keeps the provenance honest. The raw artifact was written under --compact, so all three of its buckets are empty and its summary reports 201 passed against 0 recorded; these three match the declared-derived oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-checkov-features.json's passed_checks[0], [1] and [2], its skipped_checks[0] and its parsing_errors[0], which is where they were carried from; the byte-for-byte capture oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/checkov.json carries none of the three. They are what makes the failures-only contract testable at all -- see failures_only.vacuity_note.
fixture.sha256_purpose: The recorded digest is what makes a later edit to the fixture visible. These expectations are re-derived when the fixture changes, never adjusted to keep a test green.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape -- this artifact is not SARIF and routes to the native adapter keyed by the runner that wrote it. It carries no version of "2.1.0" and no runs array, which together are the whole of the SARIF test.
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route("checkov", doc) returns tool "checkov", shape "checkov", adapter "checkov", scanner_class "misconfig"
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No shape failure is expected here, and a test asserting one against this fixture would be asserting the wrong thing. The enclosing document is a well-formed Checkov report in its object form and routes cleanly; four records inside it are defective, and the adapter rejects those while still emitting the others. The fixtures that own shape-detection failure are near-sarif-version-only.json, near-sarif-runs-only.json and unknown-shape.json.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py. This fixture is eligible material for it, being native, but the assertion is that file's and is not restated here.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant, of which harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py carries the authored copy AAP 0.6.4's import restriction requires. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted, and a test must assert the order rather than the set: a row that carried the twelve keys in some other order would satisfy a set comparison while writing a CSV whose columns did not line up with its header.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS. start_line is one of the five that may be absent, which is what makes this file's central distinction possible: a row may legitimately carry start_line null, so a defective line range that also yielded null would be indistinguishable from a record that honestly states no line.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

resolution_context.worked_example: AAP 0.5.3's first user example, carried in unchanged. Checkov's file_path is relative to the scan target and carries a leading slash, alongside file_abs_path holding the filesystem-absolute path and repo_file_path a root-relative path that also carries a leading slash. The expected path is the leading slash stripped and the remainder treated as root-relative, reconciled against the absolute file_abs_path the same record carries. Every record in this fixture carries all three fields intact, which is deliberate: path resolution is not this fixture's subject, so nothing here may be rejected for its path.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the checkov entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.runner_invocation: one checkov invocation carrying 18 root-relative -d target roots, recorded at runner-metadata.json tools.checkov.invocation_form. This is the fact that makes file_path ambiguous on its own, and therefore the fact that makes an anchor field load-bearing rather than a convenience.
resolution_context.anchor_used: repo_file_path on both rows, and on all four rejected records before they reached step 5
resolution_context.anchor_rule: repo_file_path is root-relative and carries a leading slash, so exactly one slash is stripped and the remainder is the row's path. file_abs_path is filesystem-absolute and is relativized to the scan root. The branch is chosen by which field it is, never by whether the value looks absolute -- which is the whole of the worked example, since repo_file_path looks filesystem-absolute while not being it.
resolution_context.file_path_role: corroboration only. Under per_target_directory the slash-stripped file_path is relative to whichever -d root matched, so it corroborates by being a suffix of the anchored path -- and it is, on both rows and on all four rejected records. No disagreement exists anywhere in this fixture, which is why path_corroboration_recorded is 0.
resolution_context.why_file_path_alone_is_wrong: Stripping the slash off file_path and joining the remainder to the tree root names dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile, a directory that does not exist at the root and which matches no allowlist glob, so every row would silently take in_scope false. Reading the same value as filesystem-absolute is the failure the worked example warns about: it relativizes to a long ../ chain, with nothing crashing. No expected path in this file begins with / or contains a ../ segment.
resolution_context.scan_root_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, spark_src and the checkov entry's resolved_scan_root
resolution_context.root_independence: Both rows below hold for whatever absolute scan root the adapter is given: each path comes from repo_file_path, which is already root-relative and needs no root to resolve. No row carries an absolute path in any field. The absolute values that do appear in this file are quoted evidence rather than emitted data -- the recorded scan root, each record's own file_abs_path under row_derivations and rejections, and the parsing-error entry Checkov reported verbatim -- and none of them reaches a row. All four rejections are root-independent for a stronger reason still: each is decided at step 5 from the record's own file_line_range, a field no choice of root touches.
resolution_context.severity_source: the record's own severity field, which is null on every failed check because severities require a licence and BC_API_KEY is deliberately absent. severity.resolve then states the absence rather than assuming a level: severity_native null, severity_norm Info, basis no_vocabulary. No CVSS score is consulted -- a misconfiguration carries none, and AAP 0.5.4's checkov row names severity and nothing else.
resolution_context.start_line_source: file_line_range[0], as an integer. This is the field the whole fixture turns on, and start_line_policy below states every shape it takes here and the outcome each earns.
resolution_context.cwe_and_cve_source: the closed field set guideline, description, short_description, bc_category, benchmarks, details, vulnerability_details. Every one of them is null or an empty array on every record here, so no CWE or CVE token exists to collect and both fields are null on both rows. check_name is deliberately outside that set: it is the row's message, and harvesting an identifier out of a message would put a weakness reference in the dataset that the record never made as a reference.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on both rows. A misconfiguration names a location in a configuration file rather than a package, so no coordinate can be formed -- and that absence is not a rejection: AAP 0.5.4 attaches unformable_package_coordinate to a dependency-oriented record, which this is not.

start_line_policy.statement: This fixture's subject is the difference between a start_line that is ABSENT and line information that is PRESENT but unusable. Absence is permitted: start_line is one of the five fields AAP 0.8.2 allows to be absent, so a record that states no line yields a row with start_line null. Line information that is present and unusable is a rejection, counted under a named class -- either because the first element is not a line number, or because the array itself is not the shape the field's contract requires.
start_line_policy.what_makes_this_tool_different: checkov is the only adapter whose start_line comes from INSIDE an array. Every other tool reads a scalar: sarif reads region.startLine, gitleaks StartLine, trivy StartLine, joern the reported line. So for every other tool there is exactly one way for the value to be wrong -- the wrong type -- while here the container can be wrong too, and it can be wrong in three distinct ways that fail in three distinct manners. That is why this fixture carries five line-range shapes rather than the siblings' two, and why the class a shape earns is stated per shape below rather than assumed uniform.
start_line_policy.adapter_contract: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py, _start_line. Six outcomes, and only three of them reject: file_line_range absent -> (None, no rejection); present but not an array -> malformed_record, because a structurally wrong container is not an absence; present as an array with no first element -> malformed_record, for the same reason; first element explicitly null -> (None, no rejection); first element present as a bool, or present and not an int -> non_integer_start_line; first element an int below 1 -> non_integer_start_line, since checkov numbers lines from one.
start_line_policy.class_boundary: Why two classes rather than one, stated because a reader could reasonably expect a fixture named for non_integer_start_line to produce only that class. paths.REJECT_CLASS_DESCRIPTIONS defines non_integer_start_line as "a start_line is present but is not an integer" and malformed_record as "the record is not the shape its adapter requires". Those descriptions decide the split: where a first element exists and is not a line number, a start_line IS present and is not an integer, so the first class applies; where the container is a scalar or an empty array, no first element exists at all, so there is no present start_line to be non-integer and what is wrong is the record's shape. Choosing non_integer_start_line for the structural cases would describe a value the record does not contain.
start_line_policy.no_coercion: "20" must not become 20, in any file this pipeline writes, and neither must the "20" that is the whole of a scalar file_line_range. Coercing either would invent data -- it would assert that the producer said line 20 when what the producer said was a string -- and AAP 0.5.4 is explicit that a record which cannot be attributed with certainty is rejected and counted, never inferred into a field. There is no coercion anywhere in the expected behaviour recorded in this file, not for any rejected record and not for any row: emit.py's own reader matches an integer cell exactly before converting it, precisely because int() would accept " 4", "+5" and "3_0" into silent agreement.
start_line_policy.why_20_is_the_plausible_value: The fixture's defective values are all 20, and 20 is not arbitrary. Line 20 of the anchor Dockerfile is its FROM ${java_image_name}:${java_image_tag} instruction -- the file's only FROM -- and the fixture carries a genuine [20, 20] range for it, on the PASSED check CKV_DOCKER_7 ("Ensure the base image uses a non latest version tag"). So the number a coercing implementation would produce is a real line number that a real record in the same document really does report, which is exactly what makes the coercion tempting and its silence dangerous. That genuine [20, 20] sits in the passed bucket, so it contributes no row and no rejection: the only 20 that reaches any expectation in this file is the one being refused.

cases_present_in_this_fixture.case: file_line_range present as an array whose first element is an integer within the file
first element present as the numeric-looking string "20"
cases_present_in_this_fixture.expected: a counted rejection under non_integer_start_line, no row, no coercion
cases_present_in_this_fixture.note: The direct analogue of every sibling non-integer fixture's condition, and the only one of the four defects here that is about the element rather than the container. The second element is the integer 20, and it is never read: the contract is file_line_range[0] and nothing else, so a usable value sitting one position away does not rescue the record.

cases_present_in_this_fixture.case: file_line_range present as an EMPTY array
cases_present_in_this_fixture.expected: a counted rejection under malformed_record, no row
cases_present_in_this_fixture.note: The one case in this entire fixture set where the natural reading raises. See empty_array_hazard below; it is the case this file exists to pin down.

cases_present_in_this_fixture.case: file_line_range present as a scalar number
cases_present_in_this_fixture.expected: a counted rejection under malformed_record, no row
cases_present_in_this_fixture.note: A naive [0] on an int raises TypeError: 'int' object is not subscriptable -- a second way the same unguarded expression dies, and one an implementation that only guarded IndexError would still fall to.

cases_present_in_this_fixture.case: file_line_range present as a scalar string
cases_present_in_this_fixture.expected: a counted rejection under malformed_record, no row
cases_present_in_this_fixture.note: The quiet one. A naive [0] here raises nothing at all: it returns "2", the string's first CHARACTER, and an implementation that then coerced would write start_line 2 -- a line number with no relationship whatever to the finding, on a row that looks entirely ordinary. This is why _is_json_array excludes str, bytes and bytearray explicitly rather than testing for __getitem__.

The mandatory companion. Absence is permitted for start_line, so this record is a row and its line is null. Conflating it with the four defects would reject a record that did nothing wrong, and it is carried here rather than in a separate fixture precisely so the boundary is asserted against a document that contains both sides of it.

empty_array_hazard.statement: The load-bearing case, and the reason this fixture is not simply the checkov restatement of its siblings. An empty file_line_range is the only place in the whole fixture set where the natural implementation check["file_line_range"][0] RAISES rather than returning something wrong. Every other defect here either returns a value of the wrong type or dies on a type error that a shape guard already catches; this one is an IndexError from an expression whose container passed every plausible shape test, because [] is a list and is not a string.
empty_array_hazard.expected_outcome: A counted rejection under malformed_record, and the adapter run COMPLETES. Both halves are the assertion. An uncaught IndexError would abandon the artifact mid-walk, and everything after /results/failed_checks/2 -- which is to say three of the four rejections and one of the two rows -- would vanish with it, leaving a partial parse that reported neither the records it lost nor that it had lost any. That is the failure mode this record exists to make impossible, so a test must assert the records that FOLLOW it as well as the rejection itself.
empty_array_hazard.why_not_a_row_with_null: Emitting it with start_line null would record an absence the producer did not state, and would make a defective record indistinguishable from the legitimate absence sitting four records later in this very document. /results/failed_checks/5 carries no file_line_range at all and is a row with null; if [] also produced a row with null then the dataset would hold two rows that agree in all twelve fields' worth of provenance while one of them came from an artifact defect. Counting it under a named class is the only outcome that neither drops the record, nor invents a line for it, nor erases the distinction.
empty_array_hazard.why_malformed_record: checkov's contract for the field is a two-element [start, end] range -- every one of the six captured records in harness/artifacts/raw/checkov.json carries exactly two integers, and so does every passed and skipped check in this fixture. An empty array satisfies neither that contract nor the [0] the AAP names as the source of start_line, so the record is not the shape its adapter requires, which is paths.REJECT_CLASS_DESCRIPTIONS's definition of malformed_record. It is not non_integer_start_line, because no start_line is present to be a non-integer.
empty_array_hazard.consistent_with_the_sarif_adapter: The same principle, already recorded for the same classification step in oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/expected/reject-sarif-non-integer-start-line.rows.json: a region present but not an object is malformed_record, "because a structurally wrong region is not an absence". An empty file_line_range is that sentence applied to a container that is the right type and the wrong shape. Aligning the two tools means a reader can carry one rule between adapters instead of two.
empty_array_hazard.what_the_test_must_assert: Not merely that the rejection count is 4. It must assert this record's class specifically, that no row anywhere carries this record's path with a null start_line, and that /results/failed_checks/3, /results/failed_checks/4 and /results/failed_checks/5 all still produce their expected outcomes -- because an implementation that let the IndexError escape and a correct one differ in what comes AFTER this record, and a test that stopped at the rejection count would not look there.

start_line_policy.classification_position: step 5 of the adapter's fixed five-step order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. It is last, so a record defective in both its path and its line range is classified by its path. Every record in this fixture has an intact check_id, an intact check_name and a cleanly resolvable path, which is what lets all four defective records reach step 5 at all; a fixture whose defective records were also missing a rule identifier would count them under missing_rule_id and prove nothing about this field.
start_line_policy.no_start_line_exceeds_the_file: The only integer start_line this file expects is 36, on a 71-line Dockerfile whose captured range is [36, 48]. No expected start_line anywhere in this file exceeds 71, none is a string, and none is a single character -- the three shapes a coercing implementation would produce from this fixture are 20 from the string "20", 20 from the scalar number, and 2 from the scalar string's first character, and none of them appears.

boolean_hazard.statement: isinstance(True, int) is True in Python: bool is a subclass of int, so an unguarded integer check admits True as line 1 and False as line 0. checkov._start_line guards it explicitly and the guard is ordered first -- isinstance(raw, bool) is tested before not isinstance(raw, int) -- so a boolean first element is classified as non_integer_start_line rather than emitted.
boolean_hazard.why_absent_here: The only first-element values this fixture contains are the integer 36 and the string "20". An expectation for a record that is not in the fixture would be an assertion nothing can run, so none is recorded.
boolean_hazard.cover_with: a derived fixture carrying file_line_range [true, 20], asserted to reject under non_integer_start_line with a detail naming the boolean rather than an integer

below_one_hazard.statement: An integer below 1 is rejected under non_integer_start_line with a different detail, because checkov numbers lines from one and 0 is not a line. Naming it here keeps the class's three routes legible: wrong type, boolean, and out of range.

explicit_null_first_element.statement: A first element that is explicitly JSON null yields a row with start_line null and no rejection: null is this dataset's own absence convention, so a producer using it is stating an absence rather than supplying a defective value. It is the third absence route, alongside an absent field and -- for the sibling adapters -- an absent scalar key.
explicit_null_first_element.why_absent_here: This fixture covers the absence side with the absent field at /results/failed_checks/5 and spends its four defective records on the shapes that are genuinely unusable. The gap is stated rather than left to be read as an oversight.

start_line_policy.sibling_conditions: The three siblings that assert the same class on a scalar field are reject-sarif-non-integer-start-line.sarif (region.startLine "72"), reject-gitleaks-non-integer-start-line.json (StartLine "5" alongside an explicit null) and reject-trivy-non-integer-start-line.json (StartLine "62"), with reject-joern-non-integer-start-line.json a fourth (line "417"). None of them can carry a container-shape defect, because none of them reads through a container -- which is what leaves the four structural cases here uncovered anywhere else in the tree. reject-dependency-check-* has no non-integer-start-line member at all, deliberately: that artifact carries no line information anywhere, so its adapter can never reach the condition.

rejection_boundary.statement: Unusable line information is a rejection. An ABSENT line is a kept row with start_line null. This fixture is the one place both sides of that boundary are asserted against a single document, which is what makes it a boundary rather than two unrelated behaviours.
rejection_boundary.why_the_defective_records_can_only_be_re: start_line may be absent, so at first sight a defective range could simply be emitted as null. It cannot, for a reason that is about the dataset rather than the record: a row is the pipeline's assertion that it understood the record, and a row carrying null for a range the producer did state -- wrongly -- asserts an absence the artifact does not contain. AAP 0.5.4's rule is to reject rather than infer where a record cannot be attributed with certainty, and a defective range cannot be: nothing in the artifact distinguishes line information the producer lost from line information the producer never had. Counting the record under a named class is the only outcome that keeps it visible and keeps the arithmetic honest.

not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with start_line null
not_a_rejection.evidence: /results/failed_checks/5 is exactly this, and it is row index 1 below. Absence is permitted for start_line by AAP 0.8.2, and a whole-file check that reports no range is ordinary producer output rather than a defect.

not_a_rejection.case: a path resolving outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope
not_a_rejection.evidence: Out of scope means kept and marked, never rejected. Checkov legitimately reaches such coordinates, since its reach is shaped by its eighteen -d roots while in_scope is the allowlist's answer and not the runner's. Every path in this fixture is inside the globs, so rows_out_of_scope is 0.

not_a_rejection.expected: no row and no rejection at all
not_a_rejection.evidence: The bucket decides, never the check_id: this fixture's skipped CKV_DOCKER_9 shares its check_id with two failed checks. Neither counted nor emitted, per failures_only below.

not_a_rejection.case: a parsing error the tool reported
not_a_rejection.expected: status evidence for tool-status.md, neither a row nor a rejection
not_a_rejection.evidence: Counting one as a rejection would make rejections 5 while the independent traversal still returned 6, breaking the identity for something that was never a finding.

rejection_boundary.no_guessed_line: None of the four rejected records is given a start_line, not even a plausible one, and nothing in this file supplies one for them. The values 20 and 2 -- what a coercing implementation would produce -- appear in this document only as quoted evidence of what the artifact contained, under start_line_policy and rejections. Quoting a value is not carrying it.

failures_only.count_unit: one element of results.failed_checks[], the union across every report object in either top-level shape
failures_only.passed_checks_note: Neither counted nor emitted, and no passed check's identity may appear anywhere in the rows array. All three pass on resource-managers/kubernetes/docker/src/main/dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile: line 71 of that file is USER ${spark_uid} -- the last instruction, and not root -- which is why CKV_DOCKER_3 and CKV_DOCKER_8 pass, and its single FROM at line 20 carries an explicit tag, which is why CKV_DOCKER_7 passes. CKV_DOCKER_7 matters more here than a passed check usually would: it is the record carrying the genuine [20, 20] range, so an adapter that read the passed bucket would emit a row whose start_line 20 looked like a successful coercion of the defective values rather than what it was. They are observable only through the passed_checks_observed counter, which is what makes produced-no-row an observation rather than a claim.
failures_only.skipped_checks_note: Neither counted nor emitted, exactly as passed checks are not. The one entry is CKV_DOCKER_9 on bindings/R/Dockerfile at file_line_range [34, 37] carrying suppress_comment "baseline-skipped", and it must produce no row even though the identical check_id on two other files does -- the bucket decides that, never the check_id. It carries a second load here: it is a record naming the SAME file and the SAME check_id as /results/failed_checks/4, whose file_line_range is the defective scalar string "20", and it holds a perfectly usable [34, 37]. That usable range must not be borrowed to repair the failed check. Attribution is per record, and taking a field from a neighbouring record is exactly the inference AAP 0.1.3 forbids.
failures_only.parsing_errors_note: Status evidence for oss-scan-results/tool-status.md, carried verbatim, and neither a finding nor a rejection. The distinction matters more in this fixture than in the positive one, because this document contains four rejections: a reader could reasonably expect the parsing error to join them. It must not. A rejection describes a failed check this adapter could not turn into a row; a parsing error is the tool's report about a file it never turned into a check, and it is not one of the counted failed checks. Counting it would make rejections 5 while the independent traversal still returned 6. The named file exists at the pin: it is a shell script the dockerfile framework does not parse.
failures_only.vacuity_note: The three zero expectations above are why this fixture carries non-empty passed_checks, skipped_checks and parsing_errors at all. Against an artifact whose buckets were empty -- which is what the raw artifact's --compact output is -- the failures-only contract would be satisfied by an adapter that read every bucket, and the assertion would prove nothing.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of results.failed_checks[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction
counts.raw_count_authority: normalize.reconcile.count_records("checkov", doc), whose traversal reduces both top-level shapes to a sequence of report objects and sums the length of each results.failed_checks array, building no row, resolving no path and reading no file_line_range. It reads reconcile.CHECKOV_COUNTED_SECTION and nothing else, so passed_checks, skipped_checks and parsing_errors contribute zero by construction. It is the independent half of the identity: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows would satisfy the assertion while testing nothing -- and on this fixture in particular it is the only count that cannot be distorted by the field under test, since it never looks at file_line_range at all.
counts.rejection_class_count_note: Two classes, and the split is the class_boundary rule in start_line_policy applied record by record, not an accident of how the fixture was built. One record has a first element that is present and not an integer, which is non_integer_start_line by paths.REJECT_CLASS_DESCRIPTIONS's own definition. Three have no first element at all -- an empty array, a scalar number and a scalar string -- so nothing is present to be a non-integer and what is wrong is the record's shape, which is malformed_record. A fixture named for one class legitimately produces both: the name states the condition the fixture was built to isolate, and the class a given record earns is decided by the contract rather than by the filename.

recorded_divergences.subject: the outcome an empty file_line_range earns
recorded_divergences.brief_states: a rejection, and states it twice: "insist on this one ... Correct handling must yield a rejection, not a crash that loses every subsequent check", and again as a validation criterion, "the empty-array case is a rejection and the adapter run completes"

recorded_divergences.resolution: The brief governs and the adapter was aligned to it, on four grounds rather than by precedence alone. First, this fixture's construction: it carries [] and an absent field four records apart specifically so the two can be told apart, and treating [] as an absence erases the only distinction the fixture exists to assert. Second, the class vocabulary: paths.REJECT_CLASS_DESCRIPTIONS defines malformed_record as "the record is not the shape its adapter requires", and checkov's contract for the field is a two-element [start, end] that an empty array does not satisfy -- so a class already exists for it, and reaching for the absence convention was not necessary. Third, consistency: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/expected/reject-sarif-non-integer-start-line.rows.json already records the identical principle for the identical classification step -- a region present but not an object is malformed_record "because a structurally wrong region is not an absence" -- and an empty array is that sentence applied to a container of the right type and the wrong shape. Fourth, AAP 0.5.4's reject-rather-than-infer rule: nothing in the artifact distinguishes line information the producer lost from line information it never had, so the record cannot be attributed with certainty.
recorded_divergences.resolved_by: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py, _start_line: the zero-length branch now returns a malformed_record rejection naming the empty array, and both its docstring and the module docstring's step-5 summary were updated to state it. The explicitly-null-first-element route is untouched and remains an absence, because a producer writing null IS stating an absence.
recorded_divergences.blast_radius_measured_before_deciding: The empty-array shape occurs in exactly one file in this repository -- this fixture. Verified across all eight checkov fixtures in this tree and against harness/artifacts/raw/checkov.json, whose six failed checks all carry two-integer ranges. So no other expected file's rows, counters or counts change, and oss-scan-results/findings.json and findings.csv -- six checkov rows at start_line 32, 1, 34, 1, 36 and 1 -- are unaffected. Five prose statements in three sibling expected files did assert the superseded reading and were corrected in the same change, since a committed deliverable that states a contract the code no longer honours is worse than one that says nothing.
recorded_divergences.why_not_the_other_way: Writing this file to match the adapter instead would have been the cheaper edit and the wrong one. It would have recorded, as expected behaviour, that a defective artifact and a correct one produce identical rows -- and the record that proves they do would have been sitting in the same fixture, four positions later, unremarked.

scope_of_this_file.records_only_this_tool: These are checkov's rows and rejections and nothing else. Trivy also reports misconfigurations on the same Dockerfiles, and that produces trivy's own rows in trivy's own expected file: no comparison, no deduplication, no ranking and no cross-tool interpretation is made here, and nothing in this file characterises a finding as real, important or a false positive. Two tools reporting the same location produce two rows and no comment. The sibling reject-trivy-non-integer-start-line fixture asserts the same class on the same kind of value for that tool, and the two are not compared either -- each states its own adapter's contract.
scope_of_this_file.no_deduplication: CKV_DOCKER_9 appears three times among the failed checks and CKV_DOCKER_2 three times, on three different files, and CKV_DOCKER_9 appears again in the skipped bucket. Nothing here collapses them: the two that survive produce two rows, and the four that do not survive produce four separately counted rejections rather than one deduplicated entry, even where two share a class.
scope_of_this_file.no_secret_value: No field carries a secret or any content from check_result.results_configuration. message is check_name and nothing else, so the multi-line shell text those records quote -- including the apt invocations, the pip invocation and the pam.d redirection -- reaches no row and no rejection detail. The absolute paths that appear are quoted evidence about the fixture, never emitted data, and the only literal values quoted from the artifact are the defective line ranges themselves. This tree is committed to git.
scope_of_this_file.no_inference: A record whose line information cannot be read with certainty is a counted rejection, never a line picked from an adjacent element, an adjacent record, or a default. This file is where that rule is exercised for checkov's array-valued line field, and it is why the file carries four rejections and two rows rather than six rows with plausible numbers in them.
scope_of_this_file.no_judgement_of_the_findings: That the three anchor Dockerfiles carry no HEALTHCHECK and do invoke apt is recorded as the reason CKV_DOCKER_2 and CKV_DOCKER_9 fire, and therefore as evidence the surviving rows are real tool output. It is not a claim that either finding matters, and no remediation is suggested anywhere.
scope_of_this_file.not_a_run_transcript: Every value in this file was derived by reading the fixture, the pinned tree and the authored contracts. The direction is fixed and it matters here more than usual, because the adapter's first committed reading of the empty array disagreed with this expectation: the disagreement was diagnosed and the adapter aligned, rather than this file being rewritten to whatever the code happened to print. recorded_divergences states that in full.
